notes.title: Start here: why the tests in this repo exist
notes.body: The ww6 fixture is a small finance service: it ingests cost line items, allocates them to teams by rules, and reports the result per month. Before the practice exercises, read `docs/learning/testing-rationale.md`. It lists each test, says why the behaviour matters in production, and names what a fuller suite would add. Reading it first tells you which behaviours the authors considered important, so the practice questions feel like questions about the system rather than trivia about file names. Then work through the practice guide in order and keep the source files open next to it.

excerpts.quote: This verifies that read-only roles cannot trigger mutating, high-impact workflows (`runAllocation`).

readMore.why: The whole rationale, one section per test.

notes.title: Concept: validate input before it reaches the reports
notes.body: Financial data is only as trustworthy as the checks at the point where it enters the system. If a malformed export gets in, it quietly spreads into every later report and is expensive to find. The rationale document makes this argument for the cost schema test and suggests boundary tests for payload size, date strings and missing tags. Keep that idea in mind while you read the services: ask, for every input, where it is checked and what happens to a value that fails. This habit is what the review exercises train. For example, a job processed twice ends as FAILED, overwriting COMPLETED, with `failureReason` "Invalid run transition: COMPLETED -> RUNNING".

excerpts.quote: Rejecting invalid amounts catches malformed vendor exports before they contaminate historical reports.

notes.title: Why the keyed option is the one the guide supports
notes.body: This fixture note exists so the planted demo and the unit tests exercise a complete, valid notes pack. It explains the quiz in plain words: read the cited line of the guide, compare it with the code the guide points at, and decide which option the source actually supports. Each wrong option names a real location or behaviour from the same guide, which is why reading the source carefully matters more than guessing from the wording of the choices.
